input.brief: A browser extension that checks, on the product page, whether a product sold online in India is safe and genuine: recalls, copies, fake shops, explained with evidence in Hindi or English

direction.name: The product performs
direction.idea: Software is most convincing when it is doing its job in front of you. Instead of describing features, put small, true, working fragments of the product on the page: the actual control, with real content, responding to the pointer. A colour picker's loupe reads the page's own background and prints its value. A list tool lets you tick an item right there. A type-scale plugin sets the page's own headings. Find the one interaction that is the product and make the hero that interaction; then show each further capability as another fragment at real size. No dashboard collage, no browser frame, no screenshots shrunk until unreadable.
direction.composition: Hero: a short plain headline (4–6vw, left-aligned, upper-left third) and one sentence; the rest of the first screen is the main fragment at actual interface size, sitting directly on the page or on one flat stage colour, large enough to read every label. The fragment is built in HTML and works. Below, capabilities are a single-column sequence, each a row of two parts on a 5/7 split: a two-line statement on one side and the relevant fragment on the other, with the fragments varying in size and shape so the column never becomes a zigzag of equal blocks. Fragments are cropped pieces of interface (a menu, a row, a control, a panel edge), not whole windows. One section pins a fragment while three short statements change it.
direction.typography: The marketing type matches the product's interface type so the fragments and the page feel like one thing. Headline modest; interface text at its true size (13–15px) inside fragments.
direction.colour: Neutral ground. The product's own interface colours provide the colour. At most one flat stage colour behind fragments.
direction.imagery: The interface fragments are the main imagery: build them carefully with real labels, real numbers and sensible states (one hovered, one selected). Around them, two or three real pictures of the customer's world (found with scripts/assets.mjs), never stock of people at laptops.
direction.richness: Fidelity. A fragment with believable content and a real hover state is more interesting than any illustration. Spend the effort there.
direction.pitfalls: A fake interface made of grey bars and circles is the worst outcome; if you cannot build a believable fragment, change direction. Mark each fragment's root element with the attribute data-ui: inside it the product's own conventions apply (1px control borders, small radii, a shadow on its open menu) and the inspector leaves them alone; outside it the house rules hold as usual. data-ui is for cropped fragments only, never for a page wrapper. Do not put the fragment in a browser or laptop frame.

hero.name: Sentence split by a frame
hero.blueprint: A white or pale ground. One short sentence is broken in two and pushed to the edges: the first half flush to the 32px left margin, the second half flush to the right margin, both on the vertical centre line at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 60px), medium weight. Between them, dead centre on columns 5–8, sits one media frame: 35% of the viewport wide, 16:9, corners 4px, holding a photograph or a working fragment of the product. The frame belongs to a vertical reel: the bottom 60px of the previous frame shows at the top edge of the viewport and the top 60px of the next at the bottom edge, same width, 24px gaps, so the centre column reads as a strip passing through the sentence. The stage is sticky; the reel advances three or four steps while the two halves of the sentence hold their place. Wordmark top-left; three text links and the single action as a small solid button top-right, all at 15px. Bottom-left on columns 1–4: one supporting sentence at 18px, its last line 32px above the bottom edge. The other corners stay empty.
hero.mobile: The halves stack: the first half of the sentence at 9vw flush left under the wordmark, then the frame at full width minus 16px margins and 4:3, then the second half flush right at 9vw. The neighbouring frames show as 28px slivers above and below. The supporting sentence and the action button follow at 16px. The links collapse to one word.
hero.headline: One sentence of four to six words split into two halves of up to about 14 characters each; the frame between them shows what it is about.

type.note: The pointed, circular geometry of the 1920s in bold capitals, with the same family at reading size. Suits space, science, museums, architecture and anything that should feel like a mid-century poster.

palette.name: Black and crimson
palette.note: Black with off-white text and mid-grey texture takes nearly the whole page, and the last sections may invert to off-white with black type. Deep crimson is scattered sparingly: a few characters in a heading, a slider fill, the one button.

motion.name: Masked headline
motion.description: On load, each line of the headline rises from behind its own baseline, about 900ms with a strong ease-out, the second line 110ms after the first; the supporting sentence and the action then fade up together. Nothing else on the page performs. Because headlines are two lines at most, you author the line breaks and wrap each line yourself. Recipe: 'Masked line reveal' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Lead line over four columns
sections.blueprint: Two parts on one 12-column grid with 20px margins. First, a lead paragraph of 30–40 words spans all 12 columns at clamp(22px, 2.2vw, 32px), regular weight, leading 1.2: three lines that read as the opening of a text, with no heading before it. 72px below, four equal columns (three grid columns each, 24px gutters) carry small text at 14–15px with leading 1.45. Each column is one paragraph of 40–70 words that opens with a bold run-in phrase of two or three words in full ink, the rest continuing on the same line in the soft ink. Columns top-align and end ragged at different depths. No cards, icons or dividers; the bold run-ins are the only markers. The four columns answer four plain questions: who, what, where, how to reach them. Padding is modest, 96px top and bottom, so a sheet of images can start straight after.
sections.mobile: The lead paragraph at 20px, full width. The four columns become a two-by-two grid with a 20px gutter and 40px row gap at 14px; if any paragraph exceeds 60 words, switch to one column with 32px between paragraphs. Run-in phrases stay bold.

sections.name: Sentences with switches
sections.blueprint: Four or five capabilities, each one plain sentence of five to eight words about what the product will do for you, each ending in a working switch. Every sentence is a full-bleed band 20vh tall, butted against the next with no gap. Inside, on the 12-column grid: the sentence at clamp(30px, 3.6vw, 60px) on one line in columns 1–10, vertically centred; in columns 11–12, right-aligned, the product's real toggle, built in em with its root marked data-ui, 1.1em tall so it matches the type. Off, a band is the page ground and its sentence is in the soft ink. On, the band fills with a palette colour, a different one per band, the sentence turns to full ink and a second line at 17px appears beneath stating the consequence in figures. Two bands are on at load. Toggles answer click, Space and Enter. There is no heading; the first sentence does that work.
sections.mobile: Bands are at least 132px tall. The sentence is set at 6.4vw on two lines in the left 76% of the width; the toggle sits at the right, vertically centred, with a 44px touch target. When a band is on, the consequence line opens under the sentence at 15px.

sections.name: Pinned fragment, changing state
sections.blueprint: Two columns. Right, columns 7–12: a stage that is position: sticky; top: 14vh, holding one fragment of the real interface at true size on a single flat stage colour, about 520px square. Left, columns 1–5: three statements, each in its own block 80vh tall, so one is in view at a time. A statement is a two-line sentence at 28–32px that begins with its order word ('Paste a link.', 'Then pick the parts you want.', 'Share it when it looks right.') plus one supporting line at 16px. The statement nearest the viewport's centre is in full ink; the others sit at 30%. As each statement becomes active the fragment changes to the matching state: an empty field, a filled list with two rows selected, a finished result with its confirmation. Build the states in HTML and switch a class; do not swap screenshots. The heading, two to four words at 24–28px, sits above the first statement.
sections.mobile: The stage is sticky at the top, 46svh tall, the fragment fitted by cropping to its active region, not by shrinking its text. Statements scroll beneath it in blocks 60svh tall at 22px. The stage releases after the third statement.

sections.name: Input half, output half
sections.blueprint: Two flat fields meet on a vertical edge at 50vw, each 90svh tall, no gap. The left field is the darkest palette tone and holds what the user hands the product, raw: a pasted note, a messy row of figures, a prompt, or literal code inside `<code>`. It is an editable region at 20–24px, 34ch wide, starting at column 2, 30% down the field. The right field is the lightest tone and holds what the product makes of it as a true-size fragment marked data-ui: the tidy record, the chart, the formatted reply, 440–520px wide, on the same top line. Editing the left changes the right. The heading is split across the edge: its first one or two words bottom-left on the dark field, its last one or two bottom-right on the light field, both at clamp(40px, 5vw, 80px) on one baseline 32px from the bottom.
sections.mobile: The fields stack, dark above light, each 62svh, meeting on a horizontal edge. Input text at 18px with 20px margins; the output fragment at true size on the light field. The heading's two parts sit either side of that edge at 11vw: one at the foot of the dark field, one at the top of the light.

sections.name: Founder's letter
sections.blueprint: A letter in a centred column 520px wide with at least 160px of empty ground above and below. At the column's top-left, a round portrait 44px across. 28px below it, four or five short paragraphs at 16–17px with leading 1.55, each two to four lines and separated by one blank line, written in the first person. No heading. The sign-off is the writer's name at 22px in the text face's italic, with the role at 14px in the soft ink beneath it. One phrase in the letter may carry a flat marker-colour background. Variant for a page built as an object: the letter sits on a filled paper-colour sheet 640px wide with 60px padding on a contrasting ground, square corners, its bottom edge cut into small scallops with `clip-path`, and below a row of 5px round dots a tear-off strip 72px tall that carries the email address.
sections.mobile: The column takes the full width with 24px margins; text at 16px, portrait 40px. In the sheet variant the sheet spans edge to edge with 24px padding and keeps its shaped bottom edge; the tear-off strip stacks the email above a full-width button.

sections.name: Large marks on tiles
sections.blueprint: A board of filled tiles, four across and two or three rows deep, with 8px gaps, spanning the full content width. Each tile is about 3:2, one step lighter or darker than the page ground, with no border. A tile holds one supplied logo, shown far larger than a usual logo strip: about 72px tall, centred, in the page ink as a single-colour SVG. When no logo files exist, the tile holds the name instead, set at 28–32px bold, top-left with 24px padding; never draw a mark. One tile, twice the width of the others and placed first, is in the accent colour and carries the heading: two to four words at about 3vw, top-left. Tile corners follow the page's one radius, or the page's motif shape if it has one. Tiles sit still; there is no hover lift.
sections.mobile: Two tiles per row with 6px gaps, logos at 44px tall. The heading tile runs full width first, about 120px tall. Show eight tiles at most so the board stays under one and a half screens. Names set in type drop to 20px.

sections.name: Accordion of filled tiles
sections.blueprint: A two-part row. Columns 1–4 hold the heading, two to four words at about 4vw, `position: sticky; top: 96px` so it stays while the list scrolls past. Columns 5–12 hold the accordion: each question is a filled tile one step from the page ground, with 8px between tiles, no border and the page's one radius (or its motif's corner). A closed tile is 72px tall with the question at 20px medium on the left, 24px padding, and on the right a plus sign drawn from two 3px bars 16px long. The open tile switches to the accent colour with its assigned ink, the plus becomes a minus by rotating one bar, and the answer appears at 17px, no wider than 52ch. Build each tile as `<details>` with a shared `name` so one opens at a time. Six to nine tiles.
sections.mobile: The heading sits above at 9vw, not sticky. Tiles run full width with 6px gaps, questions at 18px wrapping to two lines, closed height at least 64px. The open tile keeps the accent colour, and answers are set at 16px with 20px padding.

sections.name: First step, already open
sections.blueprint: The page ends with the product's first screen already open. A full-bleed field in the accent colour, 90svh tall. Right, in columns 7–11, vertically centred: the product's own create dialog at true size, 440px wide, root marked data-ui, with its real title ('Name your workspace'), one text field holding an editable, believable example, one two-option segmented choice and its primary button. Inside the fragment the product's conventions apply, including the shadow its dialog normally casts. The field accepts typing, the choice switches, and the primary button is the page's only action: it carries the typed value into sign-up. Left, in columns 1–5, anchored to the bottom with 40px margins: the closing line, two to four words at clamp(56px, 7vw, 112px), leading 0.92, on two lines, and under it one sentence at 17px saying what happens after the button. The upper-left stays empty.
sections.mobile: The closing line leads at 13vw on two lines, top-left, with its sentence beneath at 16px. The dialog follows at full width inside 16px margins, at true size, its primary button 52px tall and full width. The field is at least 84svh; the dialog sits in its lower half.

sections.name: A single quiet line
sections.blueprint: No footer block at all. After at least 30svh of empty page ground, one baseline 30px above the bottom edge carries three items in the page's ordinary small text size (14–16px), the same size and weight as the navigation: at the left margin, what this is in three or four words; centred, two to five links separated by 24px of space; at the right margin, the year and a privacy link. Use a three-column grid (1fr auto 1fr) so the centre group is truly centred whatever the side lengths. No logo, no background change, no line above it, no columns. Links are in the full ink; the rest in the softer ink. If the page has a narrow text column, the three items may instead sit on that column's left edge as one wrapped line. The restraint only works if the page above has already made its invitation.
sections.mobile: Three short lines at 14px on the left margin with 8px between them: the description, the links on one wrapped line, then year and privacy. Links stay in the full ink. Leave 20svh of empty ground above and 24px below.

references.name: Uni
references.idea: The product lives in the laptop notch, so the page's navigation is a black notch and the hero is a laptop outline whose notch opens into the app.
references.hero: White page with the hero as a rounded-corner panel inset 24px on all sides, filled with a grainy pastel gradient (pink-peach centre, sky blue down the right edge, orange lower-left). A black pill 300×44px sits top-centre like a laptop notch, holding only the app icon; it is the entire nav. Centred below: a hand-scrawled caps eyebrow, a two-line 48px (3.3vw) headline, two white pill download buttons side by side, one line of tiny grey reassurance. The bottom 40% is a thick black outline of a laptop screen, 960px wide, cropped by the fold, its notch expanded into a dark input bar playing the demo.
references.type: Instrument Sans 500 at 48px with -0.025em tracking for headings; Geist 16px for UI and 12–13px captions. Eyebrows are hand-scrawled marker capitals, irregular and tilted. Only three sizes on the page; the headline is just three times the body.
references.colour: #ffffff #fbdad6 #fce6db #aacbec #f9a070 #000000 — Colour lives only in the hero's grainy pastel gradient; below it the page is white and #fbfbfb with black text. Buttons are near-white pills; the notch is the single black mass.
references.imagery: No photos. A laptop reduced to a thick black rounded outline frames a looping screen recording of the notch UI; eight line icons below. The gradient has visible film grain.
references.layout: Everything on the centre axis. The laptop frame's side strokes continue down the page as hairline rules, so the mockup becomes a 960px content column holding tabs, an icon grid and an FAQ. Three short sections, generous white space, minimal footer.

sections.description: Directly under the device a segmented pill control with three tabs switches the demo. Then a hand-scrawled two-word eyebrow, a centred 32px heading, and a four-by-two grid of thin line icons, each with a two-line 12px centred caption. No cards, borders or backgrounds — just icons on white with about 100px between columns, all inside the hairline-bounded column.

A #fbfbfb band inside the same column. The heading straddles the band's top edge. One rounded, hairline-bordered container holds nine rows separated by hairlines; each row has a 12px medium question at left and a thin plus sign at right. Beneath, a two-line micro footer centred: Roman-numeral year, tiny wordmark, a three-word credit, two legal links.

steal: Shape the navigation like the product's own hardware habitat (here a black notch pill) so the nav itself demonstrates the product.
Extend a device mockup's side strokes down the page as hairline rules so the mockup becomes the content column.
Use a hand-scrawled marker eyebrow above a clean grotesk headline to add one human note to a system-clean page.

references.name: Rows
references.idea: Radical understatement: a product about simple lists is sold with a 27px headline, 12px copy and a column of small live demos, each proving one interaction.
references.hero: Warm off-white page, almost empty. Everything hangs on one vertical line 27% in from the left. A small striped-letter logo mark sits there near the top; 220px lower comes a two-line headline at only 27px (under 2vw), then three lines of 13px body about 370px wide, then a near-black rectangular button with 4px corners beside a text link with an arrow. A single grey sign-in link sits in the top-right corner; there is no navigation bar. More than 80% of the viewport is blank. At the bottom edge the first feature module peeks in: grey demo panel left, short text column right.
references.type: Suisse Intl only, weight 450–500, tracking −0.04em. Headline 27px, feature headings about 16px on two lines, body 12px. Three sizes in total, no uppercase and no display moment; hierarchy comes from weight and empty space alone.
references.colour: #f5f6f1 #e6e7e1 #1a191d #ffffff #c7372f #3aa56a — Warm paper off-white with slightly darker grey-green demo panels and near-black type; colour appears only inside the UI as priority dots, outlined status pills and one green or red action button.
references.imagery: No pictures: small live-rendered fragments of the app (two or three white list rows with dots, status pills, avatars and a visible cursor) sit in flat grey panels of fixed 368px width with barely rounded corners.
references.layout: One content block about 650px wide, offset left of centre, repeated down the page: 368px demo panel plus a 245px text column, top-aligned, separated by 200px or more of empty space. The logo mark sticks to the top-left corner on scroll. Footer is one line.

sections.description: The repeating module: a flat grey panel roughly 368px wide and 120–190px tall holding a tiny mock list (white rows with 6px radius, a coloured numbered dot at left, task title, an outlined status pill, an avatar, a chevron) and often a cursor mid-action. To its right, 20px away and top-aligned, a medium-weight heading of one or two lines and two short paragraphs at 11–12px in a column only 245px wide. Modules never alternate sides; they stack with large gaps.

The closing block keeps the same narrow measure: a three-line paragraph at 13px, then the identical button and arrow-link pair from the hero, left-aligned on the text column's axis. After a long gap a single hairline spans the 650px block and under it sits one row of tiny footer text: brand line at left, six links and a copyright strung along the right.

steal: Set the headline at near-body size (under 2vw) and let empty space, not scale, give it importance.
Explain each feature with a tiny cropped fragment of real UI in a fixed-width flat panel, one interaction per panel, with the cursor left visible.
Hang the whole page on one off-centre left edge and never break it, logo and footer included.

references.name: Elva
references.idea: The entire page is staged inside one oversized phone: the headline lives on the phone's screen while a huge out-of-focus echo of the same words drifts behind it.
references.hero: Near-black grainy field. A phone outline about half the viewport wide stands centred, its top at 16% of the height and its lower half cropped by the bottom edge. Its screen shows a warm close-up of a smiling freckled face lit yellow from the right. The headline sits inside the screen, centred, white, three lines at roughly 64px with a two-line 18px sub-line. Behind the phone the same sentence repeats at about 8.5vw, blurred with colour fringing, dim grey, spanning the full width. Corners: rounded outlined logo chip top-left, glassy action bar top-right, small credit chip bottom-left, dot button bottom-right.
references.type: Neue Haas Grotesk Display only, regular weight, sentence case, tracking -0.03em so letters nearly touch, white. Headlines 64 to 104px, sub-lines 16 to 18px, chips 16px. The same face is reused at 8.5vw as a blurred, colour-fringed background layer.
references.colour: #090908 #151413 #393938 #d99a1c #362619 #ffffff — Soft black with film grain; the only colour is the amber-yellow light inside the phone photo, which bleeds faintly into the dark around the device. White text, grey blurred echo.
references.imagery: One warm, shallow-focus portrait (video) seen only through a phone-shaped frame with a thin light outline and realistic side buttons; heavy grain; round app icons overlaid at the top of the screen.
references.layout: A single centred column the width of the phone; outside it the page is empty black except for four small chips pinned to the corners. The phone stays fixed for all 2.8 screens while its inner text and the blurred backdrop change.

sections.description: The phone frame stays pinned and centred, slightly lower so its full top bezel shows. The on-screen statement is replaced by a longer five-line sentence at about 100px, centred and wider than the phone. The giant blurred echo text slides vertically behind the device, level with the headline in one frame and sinking below the bottom edge in the next, acting as a parallax layer.

Still inside the phone screen: feature names set as centred headings at about 80px, each followed by a two-line 12px description and a tiny square arrow icon, stacked vertically and scrolling through the screen area like an app feed. The portrait remains behind as a darkened backdrop. In the capture several states overlap, so headings collide with the previous statement.

steal: Put the hero headline on the screen of an oversized, bottom-cropped device so the product frame doubles as the text container.
Repeat the headline behind the main object at several times the size, blurred with colour fringing, as a depth layer instead of a gradient.
Pin four tiny chips to the four viewport corners (logo, action, credit, toggle) and leave out all other chrome.
